package_info.package_name: Smart Scale (AEG PW 5653 BT / VScale / com.vtrump.vscale)
package_info.package_manager: Android/iOS App Store (mobile app), Embedded BLE firmware
package_info.why_malicious: The smart scale and its companion apps collect and transmit excessive private user and device data to third-party servers (primarily in China) without user consent or encryption, request dangerous and unnecessary permissions, and expose users to hardware denial-of-service and privacy attacks via insecure BLE characteristics and unencrypted network traffic.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when a BLE client writes the value 0x01 to the Immediate Alert characteristic (0x0045) while the device is in standby mode, the device processes the request, leading to a crash and persistent denial-of-service until the device is power-cycled.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This write operation causes the device to become unresponsive, requiring physical intervention (battery removal or power cycle) to recover, which is indicative of a denial-of-service vulnerability.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Standard BLE alert characteristics should not allow unauthenticated remote writes to cause device crashes or persistent unavailability.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Immediate Alert is intended for proximity alerts (e.g., anti-loss), not for device control or crash induction.
key_indicators: Device crash triggered by unauthenticated BLE write to 0x0045
Persistent DoS requiring manual power cycle
No authentication or authorization on characteristic write

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, a BLE client writes the value 0x01 to the Peripheral Privacy Flag characteristic (0x0013), causing the device to disable BLE privacy and broadcast a fixed MAC address, enabling persistent tracking of the device and its user.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Allowing unauthenticated writes to the privacy flag exposes users to long-term tracking by adversaries, violating user privacy.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: BLE privacy should be enabled by default and not modifiable by arbitrary clients without authentication.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Device debugging or development scenarios may require privacy flag changes, but should be restricted to authenticated sessions.
key_indicators: Writable privacy flag characteristic (0x0013) without authentication
Device advertises fixed MAC address after write
No user notification or consent for privacy change

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, a BLE client writes a custom value to the Device Name characteristic (0x001e), changing the device's advertised name without authentication, which can be exploited for social engineering or targeted attacks.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Unauthenticated renaming of the device enables attackers to impersonate trusted devices or confuse users, facilitating phishing or further attacks.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Device name should only be modifiable by authenticated users or via secure pairing, not by any BLE client.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: User customization of device name is legitimate if performed through authenticated and authorized channels.
key_indicators: Writable Device Name characteristic (0x001e) without authentication
Device name changes reflected in BLE advertisements
No user interaction or consent required

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
com.umeng.common.a.c(DownloadingService.t, String.format("saveAPK: url = %1$15st|tfilename = %2$15s", new Object[]{this.k.c, this.d.getAbsolutePath()}));
HttpURLConnection a = a(new URL(this.k.c), this.d);
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the app initiates a network request to download APK files from remote servers using HttpURLConnection and saves them to external storage, enabling the possibility of remote code execution without user awareness.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Downloading and saving APKs from remote sources without user consent or signature verification can enable silent malware installation and compromise device integrity.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A smart scale app should not download or install arbitrary code, especially without user interaction or cryptographic verification.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate app update mechanisms may download APKs, but must use secure channels, signature checks, and explicit user consent.
key_indicators: APK saved to external storage without user interaction
No signature or integrity verification of downloaded APK

execution_context.file_location: HTTP POST to gather.lotuseed.com and other domains

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
POST /?at=2&... HTTP/1.1
Host: gather.lotuseed.com:80
...
<binary data including MAC, IMEI, SSID, phone brand, filesystem info, sensors, etc.>
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the app collects sensitive device identifiers, network information, and user data, then transmits this information in unencrypted HTTP POST requests to third-party analytics servers in China, exposing users to privacy breaches and interception.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Sensitive user and device data is exfiltrated to external servers without encryption or user consent, creating significant privacy and security risks.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A smart scale app should not collect or transmit personally identifiable information or device identifiers, especially not in plaintext or to third parties.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Telemetry collection is legitimate if anonymized, encrypted, and opt-in, with transparent privacy policies.
key_indicators: Unencrypted HTTP POSTs containing IMEI, MAC, SSID, and other identifiers
Data sent to analytics domains in China (e.g., gather.lotuseed.com)
No user notification or consent for data collection

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At install-time, the app requests a broad set of permissions, including filesystem and precise location access, which are not justified by the app's stated functionality and increase the risk of privilege abuse.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Requesting excessive permissions expands the app's attack surface and enables unauthorized access to sensitive user data and system resources.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A smart scale app should only request permissions necessary for its core functionality, not for mounting filesystems or accessing fine location.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Fitness apps with mapping features may require location, but this app does not provide such features.
key_indicators: Permission requests not aligned with app functionality

attack_chain.action: Attacker connects to the smart scale via BLE and writes to the Immediate Alert characteristic, causing the device to crash and become unresponsive (denial-of-service).
attack_chain.leads_to: Device is rendered unusable until power-cycled, resulting in loss of user data and settings.

attack_chain.action: Attacker writes to the privacy flag characteristic, disabling BLE privacy and enabling persistent device and user tracking.
attack_chain.leads_to: Persistent tracking of the user via a fixed MAC address, compromising user privacy.

attack_chain.action: Attacker writes to the device name characteristic, enabling social engineering or device identification for further targeted attacks.
attack_chain.leads_to: Device can be impersonated or used for phishing, increasing risk of user deception.

attack_chain.action: App collects sensitive device and user data and sends it unencrypted to third-party analytics servers.
attack_chain.leads_to: User privacy is compromised, and data is accessible to third parties and potential network attackers.

attack_chain.action: App downloads and saves APKs from remote servers, potentially enabling remote code execution.
attack_chain.leads_to: Device compromise via malicious APK installation, allowing further exploitation.

attack_chain.action: App requests excessive permissions, increasing the attack surface and risk of privilege abuse.
attack_chain.leads_to: Facilitates all previous steps and enables further exploitation by granting unnecessary access.

behavioral_signatures: BLE characteristic writes to Immediate Alert (0x0045), Privacy Flag (0x0013), or Device Name (0x001e) without authentication
Unencrypted HTTP POST requests to Chinese analytics domains containing device identifiers (IMEI, MAC, SSID, etc.)
App downloads APK files from remote servers at runtime and saves them to external storage
App requests MOUNT_UNMOUNT_FILESYSTEMS or ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION permissions in AndroidManifest.xml
file_indicators: AndroidManifest.xml with excessive permissions (e.g., MOUNT_UNMOUNT_FILESYSTEMS, ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION)
BLE characteristics 0x0045, 0x0013, 0x001e with WRITE access enabled
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor BLE traffic for unauthorized writes to Immediate Alert (0x0045), Privacy Flag (0x0013), or Device Name (0x001e) characteristics without authentication. Inspect app network traffic for unencrypted HTTP POST requests to known analytics domains containing device or user identifiers. Review app permissions for requests to mount/unmount filesystems or access fine location. Flag apps that download and save APKs from remote servers without user interaction or signature verification.
